about: fx-cut kinds: the numbers behind every version of the fx-cut transition (motion-kit shelf/transitions/fx-cut.jsx; EffectCraft transition.apply is to read the same file next). 15 HyperFrames scene transitions (HyperFrames skill hyperframes-animation/transitions/css-*.md) rebuilt natively in Rebuilds/hf-demos/transitions-b (T18–T32), approved by Elias 4 Nov 2026 ("The B are also good to save"). Plain data, no code (expressions are data too: strings with ${…} placeholders).

schema.time: every t / in / out / land / window is SECONDS relative to `at`, the cut = the old shot's out-point = the first frame the new picture owns; a caller snaps at + t to its comp's frames (round), so any fps works
schema.fps / cutFrame / frames: the approved demo comp (transitions-b, 29.97 fps): its cut frame and length
schema.window: [start, end] of the whole transition (the <id>-start hit; `dur` scales every time by dur / (end − start))
schema.shots: {old: {out}, new: {in}}: where the shots are trimmed (default 0 = at); a negative new.in puts the new shot under the old one early (clock-wipe, gravity-drop, blur-through, directional-blur, page-burn): the shot needs that much footage before its in-point
schema.layers: old / new: effects added to the shot, in stack order, each {name (the effect becomes 'FxCut <kind> <name>'), effect id, set {param: value}, keys {param: track}, expr {param: expression}}; the shot's own transform is never touched (Transform effect: anchor = position = the layer centre)
schema.track: {t: [s], v: [values], ease: [one per segment: a Graph name (core/graphs.jsx) | 'linear' (hold / untouched)], offset? (position values are offsets from the layer / Transform-effect centre, px of 1920x1080)}
schema.overlays: layers fxCut adds, in order bottom → top, each named 'FxCut <kind> <name>' and tagged (layer comment 'FxCut <old>-><new>') so a re-call removes them: kind solid (colour; pad = px added on every side: an oversize solid) | glow (a radial gradient ellipse: size = diameter, colour at the centre, opacity stops 1 / 0.6 at 45 % / 0 at the rim) | rect / ellipse (shape layers: size, position, colour) | copy (a copy of the cut: duplicates of both shots (shots: ['old'] = only the old one) in a precomp 'FxCut <kind> Scenes', plain cut at `at`; pad = an oversize precomp with the copies centred, inner = effects on the copies inside; of = a comp overlay's name instead) | comp (a precomp the size of the comp built from its own `layers`, same specs). where: top (default: above both shots) | below (under both shots) | above-new (right above the new shot). in / out: when the layer is on. set {layer path: value}, keys {layer path: track} (positions absolute px of 1920x1080 unless offset; scale %: [v, v]), expr {layer path: expression}, effects (as on the shots), blend, mask ({rect: [x, y, w, h]} | {circle: [cx, cy], keys {radius: track}, feather}; layer px), matte (a solid spec made right above this layer and used as its track matte, mode alpha | alphaInverted), repeat {count, maskStep [dx, dy]} (count copies, mask moved by i × maskStep), tint (the `colour` option replaces colour; palette = index into an array `colour`)
schema.amount: one shared envelope track: every layer whose expressions use ${amount} gets a Slider Control 'FxCut <kind> Amount' keyed with it, and ${amount} → effect("FxCut <kind> Amount")("Slider")
schema.expressions: placeholders: ${refFps} = 29.97002997 (the approved comps' rate: per-frame randomness and the ripple's phase stay on the reference frame grid at any comp fps), ${amount} (above), ${i} = the copy's 1-based index (repeat)
schema.demo: the approved demo: old = presenter-micah, new = presenter-dharya (from = source s at comp 0), or new.titleCard = the transitions-b navy title card ('Part two', 'How the edit is built'; enter = its slide-up entrance at the cut, fade = its texts fade up from black as in page burn)

light-leak.title: Light leak
light-leak.looks: A warm orange Screen wash builds over ~0.4 s while two soft radial leaks (gold from the left, orange from the bottom) drift across; the hard cut hides under the peak and the light falls away over ~0.4 s.
light-leak.use: A warm, soft scene change: a new topic in a story, a memory, a lifestyle or travel beat.

overexposure-burn.title: Overexposure burn
overexposure-burn.looks: The old shot blows out (Exposure to +1.6) and pushes in 6 % while a white flash rises over ~0.4 s; the cut sits on full white and the new shot comes out of it over ~0.37 s.
overexposure-burn.use: A hard reset or reveal: 'and then everything changed', a before → after, a big announcement.

film-burn.title: Film burn
film-burn.looks: Amber, orange and red light bleeds in from the right edge, staggered by a frame or two (Add / Screen), covering the frame in ~0.5 s; the cut hides under it and the burn fades over ~0.3 s.
film-burn.use: Retro or film-look edits, a flashback, an energetic chapter change.

glitch.title: Glitch
glitch.looks: 8 frames of digital glitch around the cut: the picture jitters ±15 px every frame while red, green and blue copies (added at 35 %) jump ±60 px; the cut sits 2 frames before it ends.
glitch.use: Tech, AI, hacking, 'something broke', a punchy jump between two takes.

expr.transform/position: var f = Math.round(time * ${refFps}); seedRandom(f * 13 + 1, true); value + [random(-15, 15), random(-4, 4), 0]
var f = Math.round(time * ${refFps}); seedRandom(f * 13 + 7, true); value + [random(-60, 60), random(-20, 20), 0]
var f = Math.round(time * ${refFps}); seedRandom(f * 13 + 38, true); value + [random(-60, 60), random(-20, 20), 0]
var f = Math.round(time * ${refFps}); seedRandom(f * 13 + 69, true); value + [random(-60, 60), random(-20, 20), 0]

chromatic-aberration.title: Chromatic aberration
chromatic-aberration.looks: The picture splits into its red, green and blue channels (added back together), spreading ±80 px over ~0.3 s; the cut sits on the widest split and the channels converge on the new shot over ~0.33 s.
chromatic-aberration.use: A techy or 'mind-bending' change, a lens / camera topic, a glitch that's calmer than glitch.

ripple.title: Ripple
ripple.looks: The picture wobbles side to side (±30 px at 12.5 Hz) and breathes ±3 % while it blurs (up to 32), building over ~0.27 s; the cut sits on the peak and the new shot settles over ~0.53 s.
ripple.use: A dream, a 'wait, what?', a thought or imagination beat, water / heat / dizzy topics.

expr.transform/position: var w = ${amount}, tq = Math.round(time * ${refFps}) / ${refFps}; value + [30 * w * Math.sin(2 * Math.PI * 12.5 * tq), 0, 0]
expr.transform/scale: var w = ${amount}, tq = Math.round(time * ${refFps}) / ${refFps}; value * (1 + 0.03 * w * Math.sin(2 * Math.PI * 12.5 * tq + 1.3))

vhs-tape.title: VHS tape
vhs-tape.looks: 20 horizontal strips of the picture slip sideways (up to 70 px) on their own random beats, with red and blue ghost fringes (Lighten); builds over ~0.27 s, the cut on the peak, calms over ~0.3 s.
vhs-tape.use: Retro / nostalgia, 'rewind', a throwback or an old-footage beat, a playful glitch.

expr.transform/position: var a = ${amount}; seedRandom(${i}, true); var step = random(0.033, 0.13); var kq = Math.floor(time / step); seedRandom(${i} * 97 + kq, true); value + [random(-1, 1) * a, 0, 0]

shutter.title: Shutter
shutter.looks: Two near-black halves slam shut from top and bottom in ~0.27 s (Fast out), the cut happens while closed (2 frames), and they open again over ~0.27 s.
shutter.use: A mechanical, decisive change: next chapter, 'cut to', a camera / photography beat.

clock-wipe.title: Clock wipe
clock-wipe.looks: The old shot is swept away clockwise from 12 o'clock over ~0.47 s (Smooth emphasis), revealing the new shot underneath.
clock-wipe.use: Time passing, 'later that day', a schedule / deadline / countdown topic.

grid-dissolve.title: Grid dissolve
grid-dissolve.looks: 12 cells (4 × 3) in the 10-10 blues pop in from the centre outwards (Expo Out 1, 2 frames apart) until they cover the frame (~0.47 s); the cut happens under full cover and the cells fade out from the centre over ~0.5 s.
grid-dissolve.use: Into a title card, a list or a structured section: 'part two', 'three reasons', a dashboard / data beat.

gravity-drop.title: Gravity drop
gravity-drop.looks: The old shot falls off the bottom of the frame (1 200 px, Fast out) tilting 4° over ~0.5 s, the new shot already behind it.
gravity-drop.use: 'It all fell apart', a failure, letting go of an idea, a playful drop into the next point.

morph-circle.title: Morph circle
morph-circle.looks: A navy circle grows from the centre over ~0.5 s (Slow launch · quick finish) until it fills the frame; the cut happens under it and the circle fades over 5 frames into the new scene.
morph-circle.use: Into a title card or a branded scene whose background is the circle's colour (colour option), a focus / zoom-in idea.

blur-through.title: Blur through
blur-through.looks: The old shot blurs to abstract (Gaussian 103) and pushes in 8 %, fading out while the new shot fades in still fully blurred (a soft dissolve); from the cut it sharpens and pushes in 92 → 100 % over ~0.7 s.
blur-through.use: A soft, dreamy change: a reflection, a quote, a time skip, a calm B-roll transition.

directional-blur.title: Directional blur
directional-blur.looks: The old shot smears left (horizontal blur 90, 8° skew, 200 px, Fast out) and fades in ~0.4 s; the new shot slides in from the right 4 frames later, smeared, and lands sharp (Expo Out 1).
directional-blur.use: Fast sideways energy: 'next', a swipe between options, a list moving on, a sports / speed topic.

page-burn.title: Page burn
page-burn.looks: A ragged fire front (torn by Turbulent Displace, a thin glowing ember rim and a scorched band) eats the old shot from the bottom-right corner over 1.2 s, black behind it; the new shot rises from black over ~1.2 s, starting just before the page is gone.
page-burn.use: A dramatic ending of one idea, 'burn the old way', a destruction / failure beat, into a title from black.
